jobs.description:
CSA San Diego County is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization whose primary mission is the promotion of social justice and public welfare through programs, services, and advocacy against all forms of discrimination, including advocacy for the eradication of housing discrimination to assure equal housing opportunity for all individuals.
CSA is committed to promoting and enforcing fair housing laws and equal housing opportunities for all individuals who live in San Diego County

Position Title:
  Executive Director
Reports to
: Board of Directors

Position Summary:
  The Executive Director is in charge of overseeing the agency’s strategic vision and leading agency decisions to drive organizational growth. The duties include collaborating with the board of directors, implementing strategic plans for agency development and managing relationships with stakeholders. We are looking for an experienced Executive Director to oversee all operations, functions and activities. You will be the face of the organization, responsible for giving the proper strategic direction and implementing a high quality vision. Must have great communication skills and take a holistic approach in managing the organization’s operations with the ability to lead and motivate. The goal is to manage and lead the organization towards the realization of its mission.

  CSA San Diego County (www.c4sa.org) is a 501(c) (3) non-profit corporation. We have decades of experience as advocates for fair housing and mediating tenant/landlord issues .

•       Collaborate with the board of Directors to identify, create and implement strategic plans to actualize agency objectives.
•       Identify, recruit, train and develop a talented team of employees who can lead critical departments and manage strategic agency functions.
•       Monitor agency operations and ensure employees and business practices comply with regulatory and legal requirements.
•       Develop the organizational culture and promote transparency and collaboration throughout the organization.
•       Develop partnerships with company stakeholders, shareholders, industry regulators and other relevant parties.
•       Identify potential risks and opportunities within the organization and its environment to protect business interests.
•       Identify potential sources of investment and organize fundraising efforts.
•       Represent the agency at social and organizational events in ways that strengthen the brand and communicate the agency’s message.

Skills and Qualifications:

Education:
Bachelor’s or master’s degree in business, non-profit management, public administration, or a related field.
Experience:
Several years in senior executive or management roles.

 Excellent understanding of finance-related performance standards
 Proven ability to develop and execute financial strategies
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills
 Demonstrated knowledge of corporate and regulatory best practices
 Organization and leadership skills
 Strategic thinking and analytical skills

Salary:
Commensurate with Executive Leadership experience

To Apply

Send a resume and cover letter to estela@c4sa.org . No phone calls please.

CSA San Diego County is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

jobs.title: Chief of Staff to the CEO
jobs.description:
OpenGov is the leader in AI and ERP solutions for local and state governments in the U.S. More than 2,000 cities, counties, state agencies, school districts, and special districts rely on the OpenGov Public Service Platform to operate efficiently, adapt to change, and strengthen the public trust. Category-leading products include enterprise asset management, procurement and contract management, accounting and budgeting, billing and revenue management, permitting and licensing, and transparency and open data. These solutions come together in the OpenGov ERP, allowing public sector organizations to focus on priorities and deliver maximum ROI with every dollar and decision in sync. Learn about OpenGov’s mission to power more effective and accountable government and the vision of high-performance government for every community at OpenGov.com.

Role Overview

As Chief of Staff to the CEO, you will sit at the center of how this company operates and makes decisions. You will own the operating cadence, drive cross-functional initiatives from problem definition to resolution, and handle the work that keeps the CEO focused on the highest-leverage problems. That means being equally comfortable in a budget-versus-actual, a headcount model, or an organizational question that needs someone to push it to closure.

You think clearly under pressure, communicate with precision, and know how to move work forward with the best judgement. You understand how AI tools can accelerate serious work, and you use them that way. If you want a front row seat to how a CEO makes decisions and how a growth-stage company actually scales, this role delivers that.

Who You Are

Strategic Partner to the CEO:

Trusted confidant and advisor to the CEO. Helping think through complex strategic, financial, and personnel decisions, and ensuring they are executed upon.
Ability to disseminate information and communicate ideas on behalf of the CEO to the Executive Leadership Team and external stakeholders.
Track record of “clearing the path”. Taking ownership of day-to-day operations and cross-functional processes to create more leverage for the CEO.
Strong financial and operational judgment: able to read and synthesize P&L data, budget variances, and headcount plans to inform executive-level decision-making with clarity and speed.
Strategic thinker, excellent problem solver, and first-class communicator.

Excellent Operator

Ability to lead and drive timely execution of business critical and cross-functional strategic initiatives in a fast-paced environment.
Seamlessly break down large and complex concepts into actionable tasks and steps.
Experience building and maintaining an operating cadence that promotes alignment, accountability, and knowledge-sharing at the executive level.

Clear Communicator

Track record of effectively communicating, influencing, and driving alignment across executive leadership and beyond.
High EQ with the ability to identify the needs of OpenGov’s Executive Leadership Team, build strong relationships among internal and external stakeholders, and promote a culture of trust and transparency.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and attention to detail.

What You'll Do

Own the company-wide operating cadence: company all-hands meetings, Executive Leadership Team meetings, and quarterly offsites. This includes agenda-setting, logistics, notetaking, and follow through on decisions.
Own the company's goal-setting process end to end, from framework design and OKR cycle coordination to tracking progress and holding teams accountable to outcomes.
Drive alignment and accountability across the Executive Leadership Team, ensuring the organization stays focused on the highest-priority challenges and executes with urgency.
Triage and manage competing priorities for the CEO: synthesize complex inputs, frame decision options, and surface key insights to inform executive-level choices.
Conduct ad-hoc financial and operational analyses diagnosing business challenges and recommending tailored, scalable solutions.
Partner with Finance on review cycles and headcount analysis; synthesizing financial data into clear, actionable recommendations for the CEO.
Lead and project manage company-wide strategic initiatives; bring together cross-functional stakeholders and drive decisions and action.
Develop and document internal processes for communications, operations, and other organizational needs.
Work closely with the Executive Assistant to the CEO to ensure appropriate management of the CEO's calendar, prioritizing tasks and meetings in alignment with organizational goals.
Serve as a key liaison between the CEO, the Executive Leadership Team, and external partners, adapting your communication style to build trust and accelerate decision-making.

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree required; MBA or equivalent advanced degree preferred.
Strong financial acumen: demonstrated ability to interpret P&L statements, headcount plans, and translate financial data into clear executive recommendations.
Proven track record managing complex, cross-functional projects or programs end-to-end, with expertise in establishing systems to track progress and accountability.
Strong familiarity with AI-enabled tools and a willingness to champion AI adoption across the organization.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders at all levels.
Strong analytical capabilities: comfortable building analyses, interpreting data trends, and presenting actionable recommendations.
Demonstrated commitment to honesty, ethical conduct, and maintaining the highest levels of confidentiality.
Passion for OpenGov's mission of powering more effective and accountable government.

Preferred Qualifications

Prior experience in investment banking, private equity, venture capital, top-tier management consulting, Vertical Software, or as a Chief of Staff to a senior executive in a high-growth technology company.
Deep understanding of SaaS business models, with experience supporting financial planning or investor-facing processes.
Experience supporting a CEO or C-suite executive
Deep expertise in operational best practices and goal-setting frameworks (e.g., OKRs) that drive accountability and measurable outcomes.
Familiarity with GovTech or the public sector software market.

Compensation

San Francisco, CA: $150,000 - $200,000

On target ranges above include base plus a portion of variable compensation that is earned based on company and individual performance.

The final compensation will be determined by a number of factors such as qualifications, expertise, and the candidate’s geographical location.

Why OpenGov?

A Mission That Matters.

At OpenGov, public service is personal. We are passionate about our mission to power more effective and accountable government. Government that operates efficiently, adapts to change, and strengthens public trust. Some people say this is boring. We think it’s the core of our democracy.

Opportunity to Innovate

The next great wave of innovation is unfolding with AI, and it will impact everything—from the way we work to the way governments interact with their residents. Join a trusted team with the passion, technology, and expertise to drive innovation and bring AI to local government. We’ve touched 2,000 communities so far, and we’re just getting started.

A Team of Passionate, Driven People

This isn’t your typical 9-to-5 job; we operate in a fast-paced, results-driven environment where impact matters more than simply clocking in and out. Our global team of 800+ employees is united in our commitment to challenge the status quo. OpenGov is headquartered in San Francisco and has offices in Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, Dubuque, Dallas, and Pune.

A Place to Make Your Mark

We pride ourselves on our performance-based culture, where every employee is encouraged to jump in head-first and take action to help us improve. If you have a great idea, we want to hear it. Excellent performance is recognized and rewarded, and we love to promote from within.

Benefits That Work For You

Enjoy an award-winning workplace with the benefits to match, including:

Comprehensive healthcare options for individuals and families
Flexible vacation policy and paid company holidays
401(k) with company match
Paid parental leave, wellness stipends, and HSA contributions
Professional development and growth opportunities
A collaborative office environment with weekly catered lunches.

jobs.title: Executive Director, Brooklyn Marine Terminal Development Corporation (BMTDC)
jobs.description:
Our Vision
: To make New York City the global model for inclusive innovation and economic growth, fueled by the City’s diverse people and businesses.

Our Mission
: Creating a vibrant, inclusive, and globally competitive economy for all New Yorkers.

Position Overview:
The Brooklyn Marine Terminal Development Corporation (BMTDC) Executive Director is responsible for overseeing the strategic vision and leadership of the development corporation, advancing its mission of inclusive growth, facilitating the redevelopment of the Brooklyn Marine Terminal (BMT), and enabling community engagement and full use and enjoyment of the waterfront.

BMTDC is a newly formed entity that will lead the multi-use redevelopment of BMT into a modern maritime port and a vibrant waterfront community. The Executive Director will have a unique opportunity to guide the BMT redevelopment and over time build a team from the ground up to support the goals of this transformational project.

The Executive Director of the BMTDC is responsible for providing strategic vision and leadership to advance the organization’s mission and drive the redevelopment of the Brooklyn Marine Terminal in alignment with the General Project Plan to be developed. The Executive Director is responsible for the operations of BMTDC and the overall success of the development.

The Executive Director serves as a strategic leader, managing executive-level and external relationships, including building and maintaining strong partnerships with community stakeholders, labor, and public sector partners, guiding staff, and leading the development and execution of strategies to achieve BMTDC’s goals.

Initially, the Executive Director will be employed by NYCEDC and supported by NYCEDC staff and resources. The Executive Director shall serve as the chief executive officer of BMTDC, report to the BMTDC Board of Directors for execution of the corporation's mission and strategic objectives, and coordinate closely with designated NYCEDC leadership regarding staffing, administrative support, and City policy matters.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Execution
Provide comprehensive oversight of BMTDC’s day-to-day operations, ensuring effective program implementation and project delivery that promotes inclusive growth and economic justice
Lead RFP development, oversee competitive developer selection processes, and facilitate public approvals
Lead recruitment, training, mentoring, and development of staff, providing thoughtful leadership and establishing a clear organizational structure
Present to and brief executive level staff, City Hall, and other government partners on BMTDC development
Other duties as assigned

Engagement
Lead engagement and establish trust-based relationships with external parties, including community stakeholders, elected officials, non-profits, real estate developers, financial institutions, consultants, organized labor, and industry associations
Proactively and holistically engage local community members and organizations, labor unions, maritime and industrial groups
Provide targeted outreach to NYCHA residents and tenant associations sharing commitments and specific pathways to economic mobility
Represent BMTDC at public meetings, external conferences, and speaking engagements, sharing project commitments as relevant

Governance
Manage BMTDC’s budget and direct BMTDC’s financial management ensuring financial oversight, resource allocation, grant management
Manage the governance of BMTDC. This includes but is not limited to:
BMTDC Board of Director and committee meeting, and public hearings
Set the agenda for the various governance meetings
Serve as the principal liaison to the Board of Directors, providing regular reports on performance, risks, and progress toward strategic objectives
Collaborate with the Board of Directors to support the BMT development and ensure its financial health and viability

Impact
Leverage decision-making authority to advance programs and projects that maximize impact and deliver targeted outcomes while prioritizing shared, inclusive growth and community needs
Lead recruitment, training, and development of staff, and establish a clear organizational structure
Reinforce and refine the project’s vision, working to maximize a benefit driven, positive impact for community residents

Qualifications:

Undergraduate degree required, and a strong preference for an advanced degree
10+ years of experience in leadership roles in the following relevant fields, which could include public policy, urban planning, real estate, development, finance
Strong preference for candidates with knowledge of maritime operations, port logistics, and/or waterfront industrial uses and/or prior leadership experience in transportation, particularly in the context of large-scale infrastructure or housing projects
Proven ability to engage thoughtfully and collaboratively with community organizations, labor stakeholders, and impacted communities, fostering inclusive engagement to move complex projects forward
Familiarity with NYC government and New York State land use processes
Demonstrated success advancing and delivering complex projects in dynamic environments, with the ability to lead, plan, and execute in collaboration with diverse stakeholders
Experience structuring and negotiating complex real estate transactions, underpinned by knowledge of NYC real estate development practices, economic development, and planning policies to inform strategic decision-making and risk mitigation
Advanced experience crafting, refining and delivering written and oral communications, with demonstrated experience in public speaking and media relations
Experience in large public works projects, with a solid understanding of economic development tools and resources, public policy issues, and managing large, complex budgets and securing grants
Demonstrated leadership experience with managing large cross functional teams to advance projects from planning to execution
Ability to prioritize competing needs and opportunities
Enjoys working in a collaborative, team-based environment and has demonstrated effective management skills
New York City residence is required within 180 days of hire

About Us
: New York City Economic Development Corporation is a mission-driven, nonprofit organization that works for a vibrant, inclusive, and globally competitive economy for all New Yorkers. We take a comprehensive approach, through four main strategies: strengthen confidence in NYC as a great place to do business; grow innovative sectors, with a focus on equity; build neighborhoods as places to live, learn, work, and play; and deliver sustainable infrastructure for communities and the city’s future economy.

NYCEDC is committed to offering competitive benefits to support employee health, happiness, and work-life balance. We offer comprehensive benefits and unique perks to ensure NYCEDC employees flourish in their professional and personal lives:
Generous employer subsidized health insurance

jobs.description:
Job Description

Be Part of What's Next

Help shape the future of how millions of consumers connect with Hearst Magazines. As Executive Director, Lifecycle & Engagement, you'll define the strategy that transforms email and owned channels into meaningful, long-term customer relationships—driving engagement, loyalty, and business growth across one of the world's most iconic media portfolios.

About Hearst Magazines (Why Us?)

Hearst Magazines is one of the world's largest publishers, with a portfolio of 30 brands
that reach audiences across print, digital, social, video, audio, commerce, and live experiences. Our brands connect with millions of consumers through trusted storytelling, innovative products, and world-class journalism, creating meaningful experiences that inspire, inform, and entertain every day.

Key Responsibilities (What You Are Doing)

Define Hearst's lifecycle marketing strategy

Develop the lifecycle marketing strategy across newsletters and email marketing, creating a cohesive approach to customer engagement, personalization, retention, and long-term audience value.
Partner with Audience Growth to transition successful acquisition initiatives into scalable lifecycle programs that strengthen customer relationships over time.
Champion innovation, identifying new opportunities to improve customer engagement through AI, personalization, experimentation, and evolving consumer behaviors.

Shape and evolve the newsletter portfolio

Partner with Editorial leaders to identify new newsletter opportunities, develop business cases, and bring new products to market.
Oversee the strategy and evolution of Hearst's newsletter portfolio, strengthening flagship experiences through audience insights, testing, lifecycle marketing, and personalization while continually evaluating where to invest, optimize, expand, or sunset.
Establish a strategic roadmap for the newsletter portfolio, setting priorities for new launches, product evolution, experimentation, and long-term growth.

Build scalable programs and best practices

Develop lifecycle frameworks that can be used across brands while allowing flexibility for different audiences, editorial voices, and business objectives.
Establish best practices for onboarding, engagement, cross-promotion, personalization, lifecycle measurement, and newsletter growth.
Think beyond individual campaigns to create systems and processes that make the organization smarter and more scalable over time in partnership with Operations.
Develop repeatable frameworks for evaluating, launching, and growing newsletter products that can be applied across Hearst's portfolio.

Partner across the business

Work closely with Product, Lifecycle Operations, Audience Growth, Data, Analytics, Consumer Revenue, and Editorial to bring lifecycle strategies to life.
Help prioritize investments based on audience opportunity, business impact, and organizational capacity.
Influence product roadmaps and platform capabilities by representing lifecycle marketing and newsletter needs and customer experience priorities.

Lead and develop the team

Lead and mentor a team of 6 responsible for lifecycle marketing newsletter strategy across Hearst's portfolio.
Foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, learning and continuous improvement.
Communicate recommendations, performance insights, and long-term opportunities to leadership and cross-functional partners.

Qualifications (What We're Looking For)

Significant experience leading lifecycle marketing, CRM, customer engagement, content marketing, or newsletter strategy within a consumer business.
Deep understanding of how content builds customer relationships and how newsletters and email marketing support audience engagement and business growth.
Experience developing lifecycle strategies at scale across onboarding, engagement, retention, personalization, and customer value.
Demonstrated ability to identify new opportunities, build business cases, and bring new products or programs to market.
Experience evaluating existing products and making thoughtful recommendations about where to invest, optimize, or sunset initiatives.
Strong understanding of modern marketing technology and CRM ecosystems, with the ability to partner effectively with Product and Operations teams without needing to own technical implementation.
Proven success building scalable programs, frameworks, and best practices across complex organizations.
Strong commercial instincts and the ability to balance customer experience with business outcomes.
Experience leading and developing high-performing teams and influencing senior stakeholders across multiple functions.
This role is based in New York City and follows a hybrid schedule requiring in-office attendance four days per week.

About Linden Place

Linden Place, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit operated by the Friends of Linden Place is a preeminent example of Federal-style architecture built in 1810 by George DeWolf. During an era when the sea was America's trading highway the DeWolf family amassed great wealth, much of it through the transatlantic slave trade. When the country outlawed the slave trade DeWolf abandoned Bristol, but subsequent generations made a different contribution to American History. Perhaps the mansion's most famous occupant was Colonel Samuel Pomeroy Colt a DeWolf grandson who founded Industrial Trust Bank and U.S. Rubber. His philanthropy and political influence in Bristol, Rhode Island and beyond was a critical turning point in the town's social history and helped make the region a premier destination for locals and tourists alike. new_jobs.title: Chief of Staff to the CEO
new_jobs.description:
OpenGov is the leader in AI and ERP solutions for local and state governments in the U.S. More than 2,000 cities, counties, state agencies, school districts, and special districts rely on the OpenGov Public Service Platform to operate efficiently, adapt to change, and strengthen the public trust. Category-leading products include enterprise asset management, procurement and contract management, accounting and budgeting, billing and revenue management, permitting and licensing, and transparency and open data. These solutions come together in the OpenGov ERP, allowing public sector organizations to focus on priorities and deliver maximum ROI with every dollar and decision in sync. Learn about OpenGov’s mission to power more effective and accountable government and the vision of high-performance government for every community at OpenGov.com.

Role Overview

As Chief of Staff to the CEO, you will sit at the center of how this company operates and makes decisions. You will own the operating cadence, drive cross-functional initiatives from problem definition to resolution, and handle the work that keeps the CEO focused on the highest-leverage problems. That means being equally comfortable in a budget-versus-actual, a headcount model, or an organizational question that needs someone to push it to closure.

You think clearly under pressure, communicate with precision, and know how to move work forward with the best judgement. You understand how AI tools can accelerate serious work, and you use them that way. If you want a front row seat to how a CEO makes decisions and how a growth-stage company actually scales, this role delivers that.

Who You Are

Strategic Partner to the CEO:

Trusted confidant and advisor to the CEO. Helping think through complex strategic, financial, and personnel decisions, and ensuring they are executed upon.
Ability to disseminate information and communicate ideas on behalf of the CEO to the Executive Leadership Team and external stakeholders.
Track record of “clearing the path”. Taking ownership of day-to-day operations and cross-functional processes to create more leverage for the CEO.
Strong financial and operational judgment: able to read and synthesize P&L data, budget variances, and headcount plans to inform executive-level decision-making with clarity and speed.
Strategic thinker, excellent problem solver, and first-class communicator.

Excellent Operator

Ability to lead and drive timely execution of business critical and cross-functional strategic initiatives in a fast-paced environment.
Seamlessly break down large and complex concepts into actionable tasks and steps.
Experience building and maintaining an operating cadence that promotes alignment, accountability, and knowledge-sharing at the executive level.

Clear Communicator

Track record of effectively communicating, influencing, and driving alignment across executive leadership and beyond.
High EQ with the ability to identify the needs of OpenGov’s Executive Leadership Team, build strong relationships among internal and external stakeholders, and promote a culture of trust and transparency.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and attention to detail.

What You'll Do

Own the company-wide operating cadence: company all-hands meetings, Executive Leadership Team meetings, and quarterly offsites. This includes agenda-setting, logistics, notetaking, and follow through on decisions.
Own the company's goal-setting process end to end, from framework design and OKR cycle coordination to tracking progress and holding teams accountable to outcomes.
Drive alignment and accountability across the Executive Leadership Team, ensuring the organization stays focused on the highest-priority challenges and executes with urgency.
Triage and manage competing priorities for the CEO: synthesize complex inputs, frame decision options, and surface key insights to inform executive-level choices.
Conduct ad-hoc financial and operational analyses diagnosing business challenges and recommending tailored, scalable solutions.
Partner with Finance on review cycles and headcount analysis; synthesizing financial data into clear, actionable recommendations for the CEO.
Lead and project manage company-wide strategic initiatives; bring together cross-functional stakeholders and drive decisions and action.
Develop and document internal processes for communications, operations, and other organizational needs.
Work closely with the Executive Assistant to the CEO to ensure appropriate management of the CEO's calendar, prioritizing tasks and meetings in alignment with organizational goals.
Serve as a key liaison between the CEO, the Executive Leadership Team, and external partners, adapting your communication style to build trust and accelerate decision-making.

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree required; MBA or equivalent advanced degree preferred.
Strong financial acumen: demonstrated ability to interpret P&L statements, headcount plans, and translate financial data into clear executive recommendations.
Proven track record managing complex, cross-functional projects or programs end-to-end, with expertise in establishing systems to track progress and accountability.
Strong familiarity with AI-enabled tools and a willingness to champion AI adoption across the organization.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders at all levels.
Strong analytical capabilities: comfortable building analyses, interpreting data trends, and presenting actionable recommendations.
Demonstrated commitment to honesty, ethical conduct, and maintaining the highest levels of confidentiality.
Passion for OpenGov's mission of powering more effective and accountable government.

Preferred Qualifications

Prior experience in investment banking, private equity, venture capital, top-tier management consulting, Vertical Software, or as a Chief of Staff to a senior executive in a high-growth technology company.
Deep understanding of SaaS business models, with experience supporting financial planning or investor-facing processes.
Experience supporting a CEO or C-suite executive
Deep expertise in operational best practices and goal-setting frameworks (e.g., OKRs) that drive accountability and measurable outcomes.
Familiarity with GovTech or the public sector software market.

Compensation

San Francisco, CA: $150,000 - $200,000

On target ranges above include base plus a portion of variable compensation that is earned based on company and individual performance.

The final compensation will be determined by a number of factors such as qualifications, expertise, and the candidate’s geographical location.

Why OpenGov?

A Mission That Matters.

At OpenGov, public service is personal. We are passionate about our mission to power more effective and accountable government. Government that operates efficiently, adapts to change, and strengthens public trust. Some people say this is boring. We think it’s the core of our democracy.

Opportunity to Innovate

The next great wave of innovation is unfolding with AI, and it will impact everything—from the way we work to the way governments interact with their residents. Join a trusted team with the passion, technology, and expertise to drive innovation and bring AI to local government. We’ve touched 2,000 communities so far, and we’re just getting started.

A Team of Passionate, Driven People

This isn’t your typical 9-to-5 job; we operate in a fast-paced, results-driven environment where impact matters more than simply clocking in and out. Our global team of 800+ employees is united in our commitment to challenge the status quo. OpenGov is headquartered in San Francisco and has offices in Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, Dubuque, Dallas, and Pune.

A Place to Make Your Mark

We pride ourselves on our performance-based culture, where every employee is encouraged to jump in head-first and take action to help us improve. If you have a great idea, we want to hear it. Excellent performance is recognized and rewarded, and we love to promote from within.

Benefits That Work For You

Enjoy an award-winning workplace with the benefits to match, including:

Comprehensive healthcare options for individuals and families
Flexible vacation policy and paid company holidays
401(k) with company match
Paid parental leave, wellness stipends, and HSA contributions
Professional development and growth opportunities
A collaborative office environment with weekly catered lunches.

About Linden Place

Linden Place, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit operated by the Friends of Linden Place is a preeminent example of Federal-style architecture built in 1810 by George DeWolf. During an era when the sea was America's trading highway the DeWolf family amassed great wealth, much of it through the transatlantic slave trade. When the country outlawed the slave trade DeWolf abandoned Bristol, but subsequent generations made a different contribution to American History. Perhaps the mansion's most famous occupant was Colonel Samuel Pomeroy Colt a DeWolf grandson who founded Industrial Trust Bank and U.S. Rubber. His philanthropy and political influence in Bristol, Rhode Island and beyond was a critical turning point in the town's social history and helped make the region a premier destination for locals and tourists alike. Family descendants occupied the house for 177 years until the Friends of Linden Place assumed ownership in1988. Today the Mansion is a crossroads of history plays host to significant events throughout the year.
